t: Dose log: injection site rotation, drug level curve, and doctor's report
Log injections and pills, get a visual suggestion for the next site, view the drug level curve based on half-life, track protein, fiber, and symptoms, and create a printable report for your doctor.
Log your doses, plan injection sites, and track medication levels

Quick answer: Enter your dose now, then let the visual chart suggest the next injection site, and follow the estimated curve of the drug level in your body over the coming hours. This page works entirely in your browser with no account, no server, and no permanent storage, so everything you type stays in memory temporarily until you export it as a file yourself. Record the dose type, time, and amount, add any details you noticed, and set the known half-life of your medication so the chart updates immediately. You can also track the protein and fiber you've consumed against your daily goal, and note any side effect with its severity and a precise description. At the end of the session, press Prepare doctor's report to gather all the information in a tidy format ready to print from your browser, or export the data and restore it later when needed.
Numbers on the chart represent sites in order, and the highlighted site is the next suggestion.

Is data saved after closing the page?
No, the tool runs only in your browser's memory. You can export a JSON file and import it later when needed; there is no server or account.
How is the estimated medication level calculated?
It is calculated by summing the contributions of recorded doses using exponential decay based on the half-life you enter. The peak and final level are shown above the chart.
How does the planner choose the next injection site?
It selects the first site not used in the last four times. If all sites have been used, it returns to the least recently used site.
Can I print the report directly?
Yes, click Prepare doctor report, then Print report. Your browser's print dialog will open with a neatly formatted report ready to print.
